O.a.1.MV: Some text assertions reject semantically equivalent wording. For example, a controlled test of the v1.1.0 delivery-tracker check accepts “ON TRACK” but rejects “On schedule”, although the task requires a positive delivery status without prescribing those exact words.
O.a.1.AW: The inspected answer comparator rejects some equivalent representations after normalization. For example, “$23” does not match numeric 23, although “23.00” and “twenty-three” normalize successfully.
O.a.1.G2: The write-action evaluator in released Harbor/ARE 1.2.0 runs rejected some semantically equivalent arguments. For example, it rejected “2000” against “2000 square feet” when the task requested only the square footage.
O.a.1.TA: The inspected text comparators reject some semantically equivalent wording. For example, the license checks reject “Open Data Commons Attribution (ODC-By)” while accepting “ODC-By”.
O.a.1.AB: The public task assertions reject semantically equivalent text in some cases. For example, the refund-notification check rejects “You qualify for a refund” despite correctly conveying eligibility.
O.a.1.HB: Some rubric text checkers reject semantically equivalent representations. For example, a financial-summary check rejects amounts written with “USD” instead of a dollar sign, although no such format is required.

O.a.2.MV: Some text assertions reject harmless extra words. For example, a controlled test of the v1.1.0 delivery-tracker check accepts “ON TRACK” but rejects “CURRENTLY ON TRACK”. Adding “currently” preserves the meaning, and the task does not require a bare status label.
O.a.2.AW: The answer-equality check in released AppWorld v0.1.0 ReAct/GPT-4o runs rejected harmless added detail. For example, it rejected “Eliana Harper with 29 followers” against “Eliana Harper”, although that prompt did not require bare names.
O.a.2.G2: The write-action evaluator in released Harbor/ARE 1.2.0 runs rejected harmless additional wording. For example, it rejected “Walk with Alessia Ramseyer” against “Walk”, although no exact title was required.
O.a.2.TA: The inspected text comparators reject some correct content with harmless additional wording. For example, adding the expanded license name before “(ODC-By)” makes the comment and README checks fail.
O.a.2.AB: The public task assertions reject some correct messages with harmless additional wording. For example, inserting “under our refund policy” breaks the refund-eligibility check without changing the meaning.
O.a.2.HB: Some email-content checks reject harmless extra words. For example, a logistics email criterion accepts “enhanced expiry monitoring” but rejects “enhanced expiry date monitoring”.

O.b.1.MV: Some text assertions reject valid expressions containing negation. For example, a controlled test of the v1.1.0 milestone check accepts “Confirmed” but rejects “Confirmed — no longer at risk”. It rejects the substring “at risk” even when the statement explicitly negates it.
O.b.1.AW: The inspected movie-recommendation content checks accept required movie titles even when prefixed with “Do not watch”, reversing the intended recommendation.
O.b.1.TA: Inspected researcher-name and subway-route checks accept matching text even when the output explicitly negates the recommendation or route.
O.b.1.AB: A constructed public-task scoring check gives full credit to an invoice summary that explicitly denies the required total.
O.b.1.HB: The inspected Slack-announcement criterion accepts required employee details even when the announcement begins “The following is NOT TRUE”.

O.b.2.TA: The inspected text checkers accept unresolved candidate lists containing the required names or routes.
O.b.2.AB: The public invoice task’s scoring accepts an unresolved choice between zero and the correct total, rather than requiring a definite answer.
O.b.2.HB: The inspected Slack-announcement criterion accepts competing roles, dates or announcements joined by “OR” without requiring one definite announcement.

O.c.1.G2: Human agreement and accuracy are reported, but repeated-call self-consistency of the judge is not established; the item requires all three.

O.g.1.G2: The filesystem path checker rejects some alternative actions that produce the same valid final state. For example, it rejects a destination directory when the reference uses the full filename, although both moves produce the same file.
O.g.1.TA: The workbook checker rejects some valid representations of the requested final state. For example, 0.043 displayed as 4.3% fails because it compares raw values without considering Excel’s percentage formatting.

O.g.2.TA: The published evaluation does not establish systematic checks for unintended changes to unrelated state alongside the requested outputs.
O.g.2.AB: The rubric checks declared assertions rather than all state changes; unrelated QuickBooks changes can leave the inspected Sheets/Gmail task’s score unchanged.
O.g.2.HB: The checks miss required parts of the final state. For example, the onboarding task requires orientation-request emails with instructions and two attachments, but the email criterion can pass with empty bodies and no attachments if the recipients and subjects match.

O.h.1.AW: General minimal-answer instructions do not disclose every task-specific parser assumption, such as the numeric type expected by the inspected Venmo-total evaluator.

T.1.G2: The released CLI build uses a mutable Python image and unpinned system and Python dependencies, so tool versions are not fully specified.
T.1.TA: Setup clones MCP repositories without commit pins and uses a mutable container tag, so not all tool versions are fixed.
T.1.HB: The evaluator image uses a mutable Python base, unpinned system packages, and unversioned verifier dependencies.

T.2.TA: Required tools include live external services whose availability cannot be held constant across evaluations.

T.3.TA: Transient errors are handled, but sustained API outages still count as task failures rather than being excluded from scoring.

T.5.AW: In the default same-process runtime, agents share host filesystem permissions, so ground-truth and evaluation files are not fully isolated.

T.6.TA: Tasks depend on live services and dynamically retrieved information, so the task environment can change between evaluations.

T.8.AB: Hinted models reach 80–100% success, but sampled reviews and expected model improvements do not verify that every task is solvable.

T.9.TA: Reference artifacts and evaluation scripts are provided, but no automatic oracle solver is released for all tasks.
T.9.AB: Hint sheets help model agents, but no automatic oracle solver is provided for every task.
T.9.HB: Expert review checks task solvability, but no automatic solver or reference execution is provided for all challenges.

T.10.AW: The default same-process runtime lacks a reliable security boundary around answer and evaluator files; its safety guards are not guaranteed to be foolproof.

R.3.TA: Task prompts, ground truths, and evaluators are public; hiding them during a run does not prevent training-data contamination.
R.3.HB: Mutated handbooks reduce prior memorization, but the exact tasks and rubrics are public and no held-out test set is reported.

R.4.MV: No recurring task refresh is planned.
R.4.AW: A future hidden set is mentioned, but no recurring task-refresh plan or update mechanism is specified.
R.4.G2: Bug fixes and improvements are planned, but no recurring challenge refresh to prevent overfitting is specified.
R.4.TA: The Verified release corrects issues, but no recurring challenge-refresh plan to prevent overfitting is specified.
R.4.HB: No recurring plan to refresh challenges over time and reduce overfitting is reported.

R.8.TA: The report analyzes model failures, but does not explain the potential impact of unavoidable evaluator or ground-truth flaws.
R.8.HB: Failure analysis and relaxed-score comparisons do not discuss the potential impact of unavoidable evaluator or ground-truth flaws.

R.9.AW: Limitations are discussed, but no quantitative estimate of evaluator or ground-truth error is reported.
R.9.TA: Tool-call error analysis measures agent mistakes; no quantitative estimate of evaluator or ground-truth error is reported.
R.9.AB: Audits and reward-hacking fixes are described, but no quantitative estimate of evaluator or ground-truth error is reported.
R.9.HB: No quantitative analysis estimates how evaluator or ground-truth flaws affect the reported results.

R.10.AW: Reported performance scores have no confidence intervals, standard errors, or comparable uncertainty statistics.
R.10.AB: Single-run scores and an informal variability statement are reported, without a defined confidence interval, standard error, or standard deviation.
R.10.HB: Four trials are run per task, but no confidence interval, standard error, or other uncertainty statistic is reported.

R.11.AW: The report discusses limitations but gives no concrete guidance on how evaluator flaws should affect interpretation of its scores.
R.11.AB: Potential task bugs are acknowledged, but no guidance explains how those flaws should affect interpretation of the scores.
R.11.HB: Deployment advice discusses model mistakes, but gives no guidance on interpreting scores in light of evaluator errors.

R.12.MV: No unaided human baseline was measured.
R.12.AW: No human or other non-AI performance baseline is reported alongside the agent results.
R.12.TA: Expert task review is reported, but no measured human or other non-AI performance baseline is given.
R.12.AB: The simple-domain baseline uses an AI model; no human or other non-AI performance baseline is reported.
R.12.HB: Expert-authored tasks are described, but no measured human or other non-AI performance baseline is reported.

R.13.AW: Some assertions detect no-op behavior, but no aggregate result for a do-nothing or comparable trivial agent is reported.
R.13.G2: Model and verifier baselines are reported, but no do-nothing or comparable trivial-agent result is given.
R.13.TA: No benchmark result is reported for a do-nothing or comparable trivial agent.
R.13.AB: The easier-domain baseline still uses model agents; no do-nothing or comparable trivial-agent result is reported.
R.13.HB: No benchmark result is reported for a do-nothing or comparable trivial agent.
